meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1/1H, Wednesday 6 November 2024, P75158A). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded in the same sitting as EDEXCEL-NOV24-F-P1 so the crossover block carries identical tags. The shared block is 1F q18–q24 = 1H q1–q7, contiguous on both papers, and the marks match item for item (3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 4, 1). Coded WITH mark_split. Only q7's (Total for Question) line was lost in extraction; it is a single mark and the paper sums to the printed 80.

coding_notes: q1–q7 are 1F q18–q24 and carry byte-identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.

q9b tagged cumulative_frequency first and fractions_of_amounts second: the mark scheme's two routes both pair a read off the cumulative frequency graph with a percentage of 60, and the graph read is what the question is about.

q13 tagged expanding_double_brackets FIRST, ahead of volume_of_a_prism, even though the first process mark is for setting up the volume equation. Four of the five marks are expansion, rearrangement and solving a quadratic; filing all five under Shape and Space would misreport the paper. This is the documented topic-straddle problem, not a tagging error.

q15 tagged vector_proof rather than vectors: the answer is a ratio of two vectors and the mark scheme awards nothing for a correct answer without working, which is the proof node's demand rather than the arithmetic one's.

q17 tagged circle_theorem_alternate_segment first and circle_theorem_tangent second. The mark scheme's route also passes through the angle at the centre, and it accepts any one of three named theorems for the communication mark; the two tagged are the ones the marks are actually built on.
q12 tagged area_and_volume_scale_factors: the question moves from two volumes to a length ratio, halves one length, and returns a surface-area ratio — three scale-factor conversions and nothing else.
